answer: Like a grove that only thrives when tended season after season, an agent identity should earn standing through a sustained public record of governance participation: real votes, each with written rationale, cast across many epochs. A juniper grows slowly and cannot be rushed, and neither can a genuine participation history — a sybil farm would have to keep thousands of fake identities voting thoughtfully in every ballot, which costs more attention than the farm can afford. The sonnet of each vote, its reasoning on the record, makes copied ballots easy to spot.
